items.copy: Day 1: The Plate Method
The Plate Method
Build every plate today around the 50/25/25 rule: half non-starchy vegetables, a quarter protein, a quarter slow carbs. One simple structure — used at every meal.
Understand and apply the 50/25/25 plate structure.
Day 2: Water Target
Water Target
Calculate your personal daily water target (half your body weight in ounces) and hit it for the first time today. A large bottle next to you makes this easy.
Know your water target and hit it once.
Day 3: Protein First
Protein First
Eat your protein component before your carbohydrates at every meal today. This single change lowers post-meal glucose spikes — and it works immediately.
Experience the protein-first effect on blood sugar.
Day 4: Non-Starchy Vegetables
Non-Starchy Vegetables
Identify what counts as non-starchy and fill half your plate with them at lunch and dinner today. Volume matters here — be generous.
Recognize non-starchy vegetables and use them as the base of every plate.
Day 5: Read a Label
Read a Label
Find one packaged food you eat regularly and read its nutrition label end to end. Focus on serving size, total carbs, and added sugars.
Build the habit of checking labels before eating.
Day 6: The Full Plate
The Full Plate
Three compliant meals today using the complete plate method. Protein first, half the plate vegetables, water with each meal.
Execute a full compliant day for the first time.
Day 7: First Blood Sugar Check
First Blood Sugar Check
Log your fasting blood sugar this morning. This is your real starting line — no judgment, just data we can track.
Capture a baseline blood sugar reading.
Day 8: Post-Meal Walk
Post-Meal Walk
Ten minutes of walking after each meal today. It moves glucose into your muscles instead of your bloodstream — and it sets up Phase 2.
Feel how movement after meals changes how you feel.
Day 9: Portion Audit
Portion Audit
At one meal today, measure your carbohydrate portion against the quarter-plate rule. Most people are surprised by what they find.
Calibrate your eye for proper carbohydrate portions.
Day 10: The Swap
The Swap
Replace one non-compliant food you would normally eat with a compliant alternative. One swap, one win.
Practice making a real-world compliant substitution.
Day 11: Hydration Consistency
Hydration Consistency
Hit your full water goal before 6 PM today. Front-loading hydration prevents the evening cravings most people fight.
Use timing to make hydration effortless.
Day 12: Snack Timing
Snack Timing
Eat snack 1 exactly two and a half hours after breakfast today. Right timing keeps blood sugar from dipping into cravings territory.
Understand why snack timing matters as much as snack content.
Day 13: Full Compliance Day
Full Compliance Day
Three fully compliant meals, water goal met, both snacks timed correctly. A complete day — proof that the structure works for you.
Execute a full compliant day end-to-end.
Day 14: Phase 1 Complete
Phase 1 Complete
Reflect on the last 14 days and log your weight and fasting blood sugar. Compare them to Day 1. This is your first measurable proof.
Close Phase 1 with measurable evidence of change.
E1
Label Reads
Read the nutrition label on every packaged food you ate today. What did you find?
Build awareness of hidden sugars and serving sizes.
Day 15: Your First Walking Day
Day 15 — Your First Walking Day
Today the second pillar activates. Ten minutes after each meal, walk. Not a workout — blood sugar management. Muscle contractions pull glucose out of your bloodstream without needing insulin's help.
["Walk 10 minutes after breakfast", "Walk 10 minutes after lunch", "Walk 10 minutes after dinner", "Log each walk in Today"]
E2
Protein Audit
Measure your protein portion at every meal. Is it really 25% of the plate?
Calibrate visual portion sizing for protein.
Day 16: Make the Walk Automatic
Day 16 — Make the Walk Automatic
Attach each walk to something you already do. Finish eating, plate in the sink, shoes on, out the door. The habit forms in the transition, not the walk itself.
["Pick your walking trigger (dishes done, table cleared)", "Complete all 3 walks", "Note how you feel after the dinner walk vs. yesterday"]
E3
Sugar Hunt
Find and name every source of added sugar in your house. Remove or replace them.
Eliminate environmental sugar triggers.
Day 17: The 2-Hour Reading Experiment
Day 17 — The 2-Hour Reading Experiment
Today, take one post-meal reading 2 hours after a meal you walked after. Compare it to a reading from Phase 1. You're collecting evidence that this works on YOUR body.
["Log a 2-hour post-meal reading after your walked lunch", "Compare with a Phase 1 post-meal reading in Progress", "All 3 walks"]
E4
No-Drink Day
Water only today. No juice, no sodas, no sweetened teas. Just water.
Reset liquid calorie habits.
Day 18: Weather-Proof Your Walks
Day 18 — Weather-Proof Your Walks
Rain, heat, or a rough day will come. Decide now what your indoor version is — marching on the spot through a song playlist, walking the corridor, stairs. No zero days.
["Choose your indoor backup plan", "Complete all 3 walks (indoor counts)", "Hit your water target"]
E5
Eat Slowly
Put your fork down between every bite at every meal today.
Practice satiety awareness.
Day 19: Walk With Someone
Day 19 — Walk With Someone
Invite someone to one walk today — partner, child, friend on the phone. Accountability you enjoy is accountability that lasts.
["One walk with company (in person or on a call)", "All 3 walks complete", "Log all 3 plate-method meals"]
E6
Full Plate Every Meal
Three fully compliant plates today. No shortcuts. Prove you own this skill.
Demonstrate mastery of the plate method.
Day 20: Foundation Check
Day 20 — Foundation Check
Tomorrow, intermittent fasting unlocks if your foundation is solid. Today, run a clean day: 3 plate-method meals, 3 walks, water target, mindset read. This is the qualifying lap.
["3 plate-method meals logged", "3 walks logged", "Water target hit", "Mindset card read"]
E7
Reflection
Write 3 things you learned about your eating habits in the past 21 days.
Consolidate insights from the extension.
Day 21: Intermittent Fasting Unlocks
Day 21 — Intermittent Fasting Unlocks

The Fasting tab is now open. Read the Intermittent Fasting Guide in Learn before you decide anything. IF is optional — a tool, not a requirement. If you take medication that lowers blood sugar, talk to your doctor first.
["Read the IF Guide in Learn", "Decide: trying IF this week, or not yet (both are valid)", "All 3 walks"]
Day 22: Protein First
Day 22 — Protein First
Whatever you eat first hits your bloodstream first. Today, start every meal with the protein on your plate, then vegetables, carbs last. Same food, flatter curve.
["Eat protein first at all 3 meals", "All 3 walks", "Log a post-meal reading if you can"]
Day 23: The Snack Audit
Day 23 — The Snack Audit
Look at your last week of snacks. Were they in the window (3–4 hours after meals)? Were they from the library? Tighten one thing today.
{"snack_timing_note": "Snacks work best 3–4 hours after a main meal, and are mainly for bridging gaps longer than 5 hours."}
["Review this week's snack timing", "Choose today's snacks from the Snack Library", "All 3 walks"]
Day 24: Sleep Is a Blood Sugar Tool
Day 24 — Sleep Is a Blood Sugar Tool
One poor night can measurably blunt insulin sensitivity the next day. Tonight: screens off 30 minutes earlier, bedroom cooler, same wake time tomorrow.
["Set a tonight bedtime and keep it", "Screens off 30 min before", "All 3 walks"]
Day 25: Ten Days of Walks
Day 25 — Ten Days of Walks
You've banked 30 walks. That is not a small thing — that's 30 separate interventions on your glucose. Today, notice the other changes: energy, sleep, mood.
["All 3 walks", "Write one sentence in your blood sugar log notes: what feels different", "Water target"]
Day 26: Restaurant-Proof the Plate
Day 26 — Restaurant-Proof the Plate

Eating out is not a threat; it's a test you can pass. Half the plate vegetables (order a side salad or extra veg), quarter protein, quarter carbs, water to drink. Practice it today or plan it for the weekend.
["Plan or execute one plate-method meal away from home", "All 3 walks", "All meals logged"]
Day 27: Teach It to Someone
Day 27 — Teach It to Someone
Explain the plate method to one person today, out loud. If you can teach it in 30 seconds, you own it for life.
["Explain the plate method to someone", "All 3 walks", "Mindset card read"]
Day 28: Phase 2 Complete
Day 28 — Phase 2 Complete
Fourteen days of diet. Fourteen more with walks layered on. Tomorrow, structured workouts unlock — short, joint-friendly, designed for where you are. Tonight, rest well. You've earned the next level.
["All 3 walks", "All 3 meals", "Read tomorrow's preview in the Workouts tab (it unlocks in the morning)"]
Day 29: First Workout Day
Day 29 — First Workout Day
The Workouts tab is open. Pick Track A (standard) or Track B (knee-friendly). Your first session is short by design — the goal today is done, not impressive.
["Complete your first workout (either track)", "Keep 2 of your 3 post-meal walks (workout replaces one)", "Log everything"]
Day 30: Measurement Day
Day 30 — Measurement Day
The tape measure sees what the scale hides. Waist, hips, chest. Same time of day as your Day 1 numbers, same conditions.
["Log your monthly measurements in Progress", "Compare with Day 1 — write one line about what changed", "Walks/workout per your new schedule"]
Day 31: Muscle Is Your Glucose Sponge
Day 31 — Muscle Is Your Glucose Sponge
Every workout builds tissue that absorbs glucose. This is why exercise compounds — you're not burning sugar once, you're building the machinery that handles it forever.
["Workout or 3 walks per your schedule", "Protein at every meal today", "Water target"]
Day 32: The Rest Day Rule
Day 32 — The Rest Day Rule
Rest days are training days for recovery. No workout today — but walks stay. Movement every day, intensity some days.
["3 post-meal walks", "Stretch 5 minutes before bed", "Mindset card"]
Day 33: Second Workout
Day 33 — Second Workout
Same track as Day 29, or switch — your call. Notice: was anything easier than the first time? That's adaptation, and it's fast at the start.
["Complete workout #2", "2 walks", "Log a post-meal reading"]
Day 34: Kitchen Reset
Day 34 — Kitchen Reset
Ten minutes: clear one shelf of anything that fights your plate. Not the whole kitchen — one shelf. Make the right choice the easy choice.
["Clear one shelf/drawer", "All meals plate-method", "Walks per schedule"]
Day 35: Five Weeks In
Day 35 — Five Weeks In
Thirty-five days of decisions. Check your Progress tab: blood sugar trend, weight trend. The direction matters more than any single number.
["Review your trends in Progress", "Workout or walks per schedule", "Share one win in the community (Ask → Wins) if you have one — someone on Day 3 needs to see it"]
Day 36: Mindset Week 6 Unlocks
Day 36 — Mindset Week 6 Unlocks
Momentum is this week's theme in Learn. Read the first card today — it pairs with exactly where you are.
["Read Mindset Week 6, card 1", "Walks/workout per schedule", "Water target"]
Day 37: The Plateau Truth
Day 37 — The Plateau Truth
If the scale has stalled, read this twice: fat loss and glucose repair continue even when weight pauses. Your post-meal readings are the honest metric this week.
["Log 2 post-meal readings today", "All meals logged", "Walks/workout per schedule"]
Day 38: Workout Three
Day 38 — Workout Three
Third session. If Track A has felt too easy, this is the day to try the next progression. If it's felt hard, repeat — repetition is progress too.
["Complete workout #3", "2 walks", "Protein-first at all meals"]
Day 39: Hydration Audit
Day 39 — Hydration Audit
Check your water logs this week. If you're consistently short, move the target earlier: half your daily water before 2 PM.
["Half your water target by 2 PM", "Full target by evening", "Walks per schedule"]
Day 40: Forty Days
Day 40 — Forty Days
Most programs lose people by Day 10. You're at 40. Today, do nothing new — just execute the basics cleanly and let that be the point.
["3 plate-method meals", "Walks/workout per schedule", "Mindset card"]
Day 41: Prep for Week 7
Day 41 — Prep for Week 7
Sunday-style reset whatever day this lands on: glance at your Week 3 meal plan in Meals, note 2 ingredients to buy, pick your workout days for the coming week.
["Review the week ahead in Meals", "Set your 3 workout/walk days", "Water target"]
Day 42: Six Weeks Complete
Day 42 — Six Weeks Complete
Six weeks. Your A1C test at Day 90 is now seven weeks away — and every day between now and then is already writing that number. Keep voting.
["All rings closed today", "Write one line: the biggest change since Day 1", "Book nothing, change nothing — just show up tomorrow"]
Day 43: Week Seven Opens
Day 43 — Week Seven Opens
Six weeks built the machine. This week is about running it without thinking.
["Workout or 3 walks per your schedule", "3 plate-method meals", "Water target"]
Day 44: The Two-Minute Rule
Day 44 — The Two-Minute Rule
Any habit you're avoiding today, do just the first two minutes of it. Starting is the whole battle.
["Pick the habit you least feel like doing", "Do its first two minutes", "Log everything as usual"]
Day 45: Level 3: The Momentum Maker
Day 45 — Level 3: The Momentum Maker
Forty-five days. Your body is producing measurably different insulin responses than it did six weeks ago. That is physiology, not motivation.
["Check your new level on your Profile", "Log a post-meal reading today", "Workout or walks per schedule"]
Day 46: Protein Check
Day 46 — Protein Check
Protein protects muscle while you lose fat. Palm-sized portion at every meal, no exceptions today.
["Protein at all 3 meals", "Eat protein first at dinner", "Water target"]
Day 47: The Grocery Rewrite
Day 47 — The Grocery Rewrite
Your plate has changed; make sure your list has too. Build next week's list from your Week 4 meal plan.
["Open Meals → Shopping List", "Note 3 staples you now buy that you didn't on Day 1", "Walks or workout per schedule"]
Day 48: Sit Less Between Meals
Day 48 — Sit Less Between Meals
Break up every hour of sitting with two minutes of movement. It measurably improves glucose disposal beyond your walks.
["Stand or move 2 minutes every waking hour", "3 walks or workout", "Mindset: re-read any card you liked"]
Day 49: Seven Weeks Done
Day 49 — Seven Weeks Done
Look at your Progress trends. The direction is the story; single readings are just letters in it.
["Review blood sugar trend", "Review weight trend", "One line in notes: the trend you're proudest of"]
Day 50: Fifty
Day 50 — Fifty
Fifty days of showing up. Today, tell one person what you're doing and why. Saying it out loud makes it real.
["Tell one person about your program", "3 meals, all plate-method", "Walks or workout"]
Day 51: The Restaurant Test, Level 2
Day 51 — The Restaurant Test, Level 2
Order out or plan to — but this time, don't look at the menu until you've decided: half veg, quarter protein, quarter carbs, water.
["Execute or plan one eating-out plate-method meal", "Log it honestly", "Water target"]
Day 52: Sleep Audit
Day 52 — Sleep Audit
Same wake time daily is the strongest lever on sleep quality — and sleep quality moves insulin sensitivity.
["Set one wake time for the next 7 days", "Screens off 30 min before bed tonight", "Walks or workout"]
Day 53: Snack Discipline Check
Day 53 — Snack Discipline Check
Are snacks still in the 3–4 hour window, still from the library? Drift happens quietly. Tighten today.
["Both snacks in the window", "Both snacks from the Snack Library", "Log a post-meal reading"]
Day 54: Strength Is Glucose Storage
Day 54 — Strength Is Glucose Storage
Every rep builds tissue that absorbs sugar. If today is a workout day, add one extra set to one exercise.
["Workout (+1 set on one exercise) or 3 walks", "Protein at all meals", "Water target"]
Day 55: The Comparison Trap
Day 55 — The Comparison Trap
Someone else's Day 200 is not your Day 55. Your only comparison is your own Day 1 — and you're winning that one.
["Read your Day 1 blood sugar vs today's latest", "Mindset card", "Walks or workout"]
Day 56: Eight Weeks
Day 56 — Eight Weeks
Two months in the books. Rest well tonight; measurement week is coming.
["All rings closed today", "One line: what's easier now than on Day 1", "Prep tape measure for Day 60"]
Day 57: Week Nine Opens
Day 57 — Week Nine Opens
This week ends with your Month 2 measurement. Nothing new — just clean execution.
["3 plate-method meals", "Walks or workout", "Water target"]
Day 58: Vegetables First
Day 58 — Vegetables First
Eat the vegetables on your plate before anything else today. Order of eating changes the glucose curve — same food, better numbers.
["Vegetables first at all 3 meals", "Log a 2-hour post-meal reading", "Walks or workout"]
Day 59: Check Your Supplements
Day 59 — Check Your Supplements
Month 2 additions may now be unlocked in your Supplements tab. Read before you buy; add one thing at a time.
["Open the Supplements tab and read what's unlocked", "Confirm your daily pack habit is still daily", "Walks or workout"]
Day 60: Month 2 Measurement Day
Day 60 — Month 2 Measurement Day
The tape tells the truth the scale hides. Same time, same conditions as Day 1 and Day 30.
["Log waist, hips, chest in Progress", "Compare with Day 30 — write one line", "Weigh in if it's your weigh day"]
Day 61: Read Your Own Data
Day 61 — Read Your Own Data
You now have two months of readings. Find your best week — then figure out what you did that week.
["Open Progress → Blood Sugar, find your best 7-day stretch", "Write down what was different that week", "Walks or workout"]
Day 62: Repeat Your Best Week
Day 62 — Repeat Your Best Week
Whatever you found yesterday — sleep, walks, meal timing — do that today on purpose.
["Execute yesterday's finding", "3 plate-method meals", "Water target"]
Day 63: Nine Weeks
Day 63 — Nine Weeks
Thirty days to your A1C test window. Every day between now and Day 90 is already writing that number.
["All rings today", "Book or plan your Day 90 A1C test (lab, pharmacy, or home kit)", "Mindset card"]
Day 64: The Cheat Meal Check
Day 64 — The Cheat Meal Check
If you use the weekly cheat meal: one meal, last of the day, fast begins after. If you haven't needed it — that's information too.
["Review your cheat meal pattern this month", "Plan (or consciously skip) this week's", "Walks or workout"]
Day 65: Hydration Before Hunger
Day 65 — Hydration Before Hunger
Half of casual hunger is thirst wearing a costume. Today: a full glass of water before every meal and snack.
["Water before all meals and snacks", "Hit the full water target by evening", "Walks or workout"]
Day 66: Move After Dinner, Always
Day 66 — Move After Dinner, Always
Dinner is the meal most likely to be followed by sitting. Guard the dinner walk like it's medicine — because it is.
["Dinner walk, no exceptions today", "Log a bedtime reading if you can", "Protein first at dinner"]
Day 67: Teach the Snack Window
Day 67 — Teach the Snack Window
Explain to someone why you snack 3–4 hours after meals. Teaching it locks it in.
["Explain the snack window to one person", "Keep both snacks in the window", "Walks or workout"]
Day 68: The Kitchen Sweep, Round 2
Day 68 — The Kitchen Sweep, Round 2
One more shelf. If it fights your plate, it doesn't live at eye level.
["Clear or rearrange one shelf", "3 plate-method meals", "Water target"]
Day 69: Stress Is a Blood Sugar Input
Day 69 — Stress Is a Blood Sugar Input
Stress hormones raise glucose without a bite of food. Ten slow breaths, twice today — it's not soft, it's metabolic.
["Two 10-breath pauses (morning, evening)", "Mindset card", "Walks or workout"]
Day 70: Ten Weeks
Day 70 — Ten Weeks
Seventy days. Twenty to the test. Tonight, rest on purpose.
["All rings closed", "One line: the habit that now runs on autopilot", "Early night"]
Day 71: Week Eleven Opens
Day 71 — Week Eleven Opens
The work now is protection: protect the walks, the plate, the sleep. Nothing new until the test.
["3 plate-method meals", "Walks or workout", "Water target"]
Day 72: Fiber Count
Day 72 — Fiber Count
Fiber slows carbohydrate absorption. Today, make half your plate vegetables at ALL three meals — no skipping lunch's veg.
["Half-plate vegetables ×3", "Log a post-meal reading", "Walks or workout"]
Day 73: Your Why, Revisited
Day 73 — Your Why, Revisited
Write one sentence: why you started. Then one more: why you're still here. They may not be the same sentence anymore.
["Write both sentences in your notes", "Mindset card", "Walks or workout"]
Day 74: Portion Honesty Day
Day 74 — Portion Honesty Day
Measure your carb quarter today — actually measure it once. Eyes drift over ten weeks; recalibrate them.
["Measure the carb portion at one meal", "3 plate-method meals", "Water target"]
Day 75: Seventy-Five
Day 75 — Seventy-Five
Three quarters of the way to the test. If your readings have plateaued, hold steady — A1C reflects the average, and your average is transformed.
["Log a fasting reading", "Walks or workout", "One encouraging comment or win reaction in Ask"]
Day 76: The Sleep-Sugar Link, Applied
Day 76 — The Sleep-Sugar Link, Applied
Tonight is a perfect-sleep rehearsal: cool room, no screens 30 minutes out, same wake time tomorrow.
["Execute the sleep protocol tonight", "Compare tomorrow's fasting reading to your average", "Walks or workout"]
Day 77: Eleven Weeks
Day 77 — Eleven Weeks
Thirteen days out. Keep the machine boring and consistent.
["All rings closed", "Water target", "One line: what you'll tell your doctor at the test"]
Day 78: Week Twelve Opens
Day 78 — Week Twelve Opens
Test-prep week one. Nothing exotic — A1C can't be crammed for. It can only be earned, and you've been earning it for 78 days.
["3 plate-method meals", "Walks or workout", "Water target"]
Day 79: Walk Streak Guard
Day 79 — Walk Streak Guard
All three post-meal walks, every day, through the test. This is the highest-leverage habit you own.
["3/3 walks today", "Protein first at all meals", "Log a post-meal reading"]
Day 80: Eighty
Day 80 — Eighty
Ten days. Confirm your A1C test plan: where, when, fasting requirements if any.
["Confirm test date and location", "Note it in your calendar", "Walks or workout"]
Day 81: The Question List
Day 81 — The Question List
Write the three questions you'll ask your doctor when the result comes. Bring data, ask better questions, get better care.
["Write 3 doctor questions", "Print or open your Progress report (Print for my doctor)", "Walks or workout"]
Day 82: Steady
Day 82 — Steady
No experiments this week. Same meals that have worked, same walks, same sleep.
["Repeat a proven day from your best week", "All rings", "Water target"]
Day 83: Gratitude Rep
Day 83 — Gratitude Rep
Note three things your body can do today that it struggled with on Day 1. Energy counts. Sleep counts. Stairs count.
["Write the three things", "Mindset card", "Walks or workout"]
Day 84: Twelve Weeks
Day 84 — Twelve Weeks
Six days out. You've done 84 days of work for a 5-minute blood draw. Let it come.
["All rings closed", "Early night", "One line: predict your A1C, honestly"]
Day 85: Final Approach
Day 85 — Final Approach
Keep it boring. Boring is what reversal looks like from the inside.
["3 plate-method meals", "3/3 walks", "Water target"]
Day 86: Data Package Day
Day 86 — Data Package Day
Generate your doctor report and review it yourself first. You should walk in knowing your story better than anyone.
["Open Progress → Print report for my doctor", "Review your 90-day trends", "Walks or workout"]
Day 87: The Night Before Matters
Day 87 — The Night Before Matters
Whatever your test day is this week: the dinner before should be a textbook plate, followed by the walk, followed by real sleep.
["Textbook plate-method dinner", "Dinner walk", "Sleep protocol tonight"]
Day 88: Almost
Day 88 — Almost
Two days. Hold the line.
["All rings closed", "Water target", "Mindset card"]
Day 89: Eve
Day 89 — Eve
Tomorrow is Day 90. Whatever the number says, it will be lower than the trajectory you were on 89 days ago — and that trajectory change is the entire point.
["All rings closed", "Confirm tomorrow's plan (test + measurement)", "Early night"]
Day 90: Test Day: The Shifter
Day 90 — Test Day: The Shifter

Level 4. Get the A1C drawn this week if not today, log your Month 3 measurements, and enter the result in Progress the moment you have it. Then come tell the community — someone on Day 3 needs to see what Day 90 looks like.
["A1C test done or scheduled this week", "Log Month 3 measurements", "Enter A1C in Progress when received; share the moment in Ask → Wins"]
Day 91: The Number Arrives
Day 91 — The Number Arrives
Your A1C result is a photograph of the last three months, not a verdict on your future. Whatever it says, it was written by the days you already lived — and the next one is being written now.
["Enter your A1C result in Progress when you have it", "Compare it to your Day 1 number", "Write one line: what you expected vs. what you got"]
Day 92: Reading It Honestly
Day 92 — Reading It Honestly
Below 6.5% is the remission threshold. Between 5.7 and 6.4 is the pre-diabetes range. Above 6.5 means the work continues. All three are information, not identity.
["Read where your number falls", "Note what your doctor said, if you've spoken", "All rings closed today"]
Day 93: If It Dropped
Day 93 — If It Dropped
A falling A1C means your body responded. That response is repeatable — it came from meals, walks, and sleep, and all three are still available to you tomorrow.
["Name the single habit you were most consistent with", "Do that one deliberately today", "Log a fasting reading"]
Day 94: If It Didn't Drop Much
Day 94 — If It Didn't Drop Much

Some bodies move slower. Longer diabetes duration, certain medications, and sleep debt all blunt the response. Slow is not stopped, and the honest metric this month is your post-meal readings, not the lab.
["Log two post-meal readings today", "Compare them to your Phase 1 readings", "Walks or workout per your schedule"]
Day 95: The Doctor Conversation
Day 95 — The Doctor Conversation
If your numbers have improved, your medication needs may have changed. Only your doctor can make that call. Book the conversation and bring your data.
["Book or plan a doctor appointment", "Print your Progress report to bring with you", "Never adjust any medication on your own"]
Day 96: What to Ask
Day 96 — What to Ask
Good questions get better care. Ask: has anything changed enough to review my medication? What number are we aiming for next? What would you want to see in three months?
["Write your three questions down", "Add them to your phone notes for the appointment", "All meals plate-method"]
Day 97: Back to Basics Week
Day 97 — Back to Basics Week
No new tactics for the next seven days. Just the four rings, cleanly, every day. Consolidation is what makes a result durable.
["All four rings closed", "3 plate-method meals", "Water target"]
Day 98: The Meal You Never Get Tired Of
Day 98 — The Meal You Never Get Tired Of
Every sustainable eater has three or four meals they can make without thinking. Name yours today — that list is your safety net on hard days.
["Write down your three go-to meals", "Cook one of them today", "Walks or workout"]
Day 99: Protein Audit
Day 99 — Protein Audit
Muscle protects glucose control and protects you as you age. Palm-sized protein at every meal, no exceptions today.
["Protein at all 3 meals", "Protein first at dinner", "Log a post-meal reading"]

Day 100 — One Hundred Days
A hundred days ago this was a plan. Today it's a routine. Tell someone what changed — saying it out loud makes it real, and someone listening may need to hear it.
["Tell one person what's different since Day 1", "Share a win in Ask if you have one", "All rings closed"]
Day 101: Week Fifteen Opens
Day 101 — Week Fifteen Opens
The work now is protection. Protect the walks, the plate, the sleep. Nothing new until Day 120.
["3 plate-method meals", "Walks or workout per schedule", "Water target"]

Day 102 — The Sunday Reset, Any Day
Look at the week ahead. Pick your workout days, note two ingredients to buy, and decide which meal you'll repeat.
["Review the week in Meals", "Set your movement days", "Water target"]

Day 103 — Sleep Is Still a Lever

["Execute your sleep protocol tonight", "Compare tomorrow's fasting reading to your average", "Walks or workout"]

Order changes the curve. Vegetables, then protein, then carbs — same food, flatter response.
["Vegetables first at all 3 meals", "Log a 2-hour post-meal reading", "All rings"]

Day 105 — Stress Raises Glucose Without Food
Stress hormones lift blood sugar with nothing on the plate. Two slow-breathing pauses today. It's not soft — it's metabolic.
["Two 10-breath pauses, morning and evening", "Mindset card", "Walks or workout"]
Day 106: The Restaurant Test, Mastered
Day 106 — The Restaurant Test, Mastered
You've done this before. Half vegetables, quarter protein, quarter carbs, water. Order without opening a negotiation with yourself.
["One plate-method meal away from home, planned or executed", "Log it honestly", "All rings"]
Day 107: Fifteen Weeks
Day 107 — Fifteen Weeks
Check your trends, not your last reading. Direction is the story.
["Review blood sugar and weight trends in Progress", "Write one line: the trend you're proudest of", "All rings"]
Day 108: Movement You'd Do Anyway
Day 108 — Movement You'd Do Anyway

["Do one form of movement you actually enjoy", "Log it", "Water target"]
Day 109: The Hydration Check
Day 109 — The Hydration Check

Supplements and diabetes: questions to ask first
You do not need supplements to use DRM.

Research has tested many supplements for Type 2 diabetes. For most supplements, there is not enough reliable evidence to show that they help manage diabetes or its complications. A result from one product or study may not apply to a different brand, formula, or dose.

Supplements can cause side effects. Some can interact with diabetes medicines, affect lab tests, or create extra risk for people with kidney disease or another health condition. “Natural” does not always mean safe.
Never use a supplement instead of prescribed diabetes care, and never stop or change medicine because of a supplement claim.
• What am I hoping this supplement will help with?

Bring a list or photos of every supplement and medicine you use. Include the product name, ingredients, dose, and how often you take it. A prescriber or pharmacist can review the complete list with you.
DRM does not sell, prescribe, or require supplements.

Fasting blood sugar under 100 mg/dL (5.6 mmol/L) is normal. 100–125 mg/dL (5.6–6.9 mmol/L) is pre-diabetic. 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) and above is diabetic. Post-meal targets are under 140 mg/dL (7.8 mmol/L) at two hours. Trends matter more than single readings.

Snacks bridge the gap between meals so your blood sugar never crashes into cravings. Pair protein with fiber: a boiled egg and cucumber, Greek yogurt and berries, almonds and an apple. Snacks work best 3–4 hours after a main meal, and are mainly for bridging gaps longer than 5 hours.
